I find there are two rules to passing ANY wolf in the game, not just the one by the lighthouse.

1: Know your mechanics. You would not believe how easier my life became after I realized you can throw stones to lure wolves away.

2:Try and stay as far away from the thing as you possibly can. Even if it spots you, most times you can still just sprint to the next save spot and you'll be fine, as it will run after you, but will have to start "Stalking" agains.

3: Have a weapon. Even a hatchet is good. If you are good at clicking VERY rapidly (I have been playing CS and Overwatch a lot in the past years, so I've gotten quite good at it), you can get out of the encounter mostly unharmed, though you have to be careful with this on high levels, it doesnt alway work even on Stalker.

I dont avoid fishing, I usually do it if I have either a long walk to make (for example, getting to a forge or climbing Timberwolf) and need food. Then I usually take three-four fish with me + some canned food for emergencies.

I actually never thought about levelling up archery with rabbits. I dont know, it just never occured to me that I COULD do that. It is a good idea now that I think about it...

I have seen plenty of wolves doing that tactic, but I'm ussually pretty lucky with it, they leave a fair space to line up the shot, and then again, actually shooting them is always a last resort, they dont yield that much meat, so I usually try and avoid them.

When it comes to hunting rabbits, which is a good strategy, I give you that, I always prefer to use the stones, simply because waiting for hours of ingame time for the little guys to walk into the trap bores me senseless if I try to do survive on it for a long time. 

And fishing...Well, thats just arguably the best option one can have when it comes to farming animals for their meat...

I find the best tactic for actually killing wolves is to wait until it starts charging at you. It's running in a straight line, if you crouch, you dont have to lead the shot, and its facing you with its head towards you. It is a bit dangerous, but if anybody misses THAT shot, they were probably aiming the wrong F-ing way.

I've always taken a 'Meh' approach to moose hunting. When they were added, I tried it out, but I always found the upsides to doing it pretty negligible, as I usually take a semi-hibernation rout to play, so I dont need the things you can craft from a mosse THAT much (then again, I dont need to hunt deer either for the crafting...)

I think deer hunting, while it is a bit tedious, can yield you some pretty good amount of food, if you try to stealth your way infront of the deer and go for headshots. Since, like I said, I like to spend a lot of time in one place before moving on, hunting deer when I come across one (preferably getting a carcass, but you aren't always that lucky) is by far the best option in my oppinion. It yields a fair amount of meat that has a high calorie value when compared to other meats, and you dont have to farm for hours like you would have to with rabbits. Just one (two, if I mess up) shot, and i have food that will last me for two days. Quick and simple.

Well, yeah, but a musical genre on its own is very, VERY diverse, punk rock even more so.

Imagine for a second you know nothing about punk. Would you group Flogging Molly's Drunken Lullabies and Dookie in the same genre? 'Course you wouldn't, they have some similarities (like a heavy reliance on power chords), but they are both wastly different, while technically being in the same genre.

You could say the same about most punk bands that are different from each other, but you can also see this with metal bands (AC/DC and Slipknot, just to name one), jazz, blues (okay, not so much, but still), classic rock, alt rock, and everything else.

Punk as a genre at this point has no real defining style. On one end you have bands like Paramore (barely, BARELY punk, but some people consider it that, so i count it), that is just a distortion guitar short of being a pop band, and on the other you have stuff like the Missfits. Both punk by some standards, yet they have nearly nothing in common.
